text: dsh-science-workbench 是面向生物信息分析的 DSH Web 工作台，通过九个 bio_* 工具创建项目、运行 Python/R 分析 cell，并把脚本、参数、种子、输入输出哈希和环境快照记入 manifest。它会发现并预览图表，支持对产物添加结构化反馈、编辑代码派生重跑、查看项目历史和标记最终 cell；浏览器界面提供项目与 cell 搜索、目录选择及内联图预览。适合需要反复分析、出图和追溯结果的研究者；需本机可用的 Python 或 R 环境，不需要插件 API key。

A DSH bioinformatics workbench: bio_* tools run Python/R cells and record parameters, seeds, hashes and environment in a manifest. The web UI previews figures, captures feedback, reruns edited cells with lineage, and searches projects and cells. Requires local Python or R; no plugin API key.
我想让生信分析脚本每次运行都留下输入、参数和结果的记录。
有没有办法在 DSH 里逐步跑 Python 或 R 分析并直接查看图？
我需要根据图表反馈改代码，再生成一个能追溯来源的新版本。
怎样把研究项目的分析 cell、数据产物和运行环境整理在一个账本里？
想快速找回之前的分析项目或某个 cell，并检查它产出了什么。
I want each analysis run to record its inputs, parameters, seed, and outputs for later review.
How can I rerun an edited analysis cell and keep a clear version lineage?
I need a DSH workspace that previews generated figures and records feedback on them.
Can I browse projects and search notebook cells from a web interface?
I want project artifacts and their provenance organized in a manifest with local commits.
dsh-science-workbench 的功能「可复现分析 cell」：通过 bio_run_cell 执行自包含 Python/R 脚本，并记录参数、种子、输入输出及产物哈希。
dsh-science-workbench 的功能「反馈后派生重跑」：为图表添加结构化反馈，再用编辑后的代码重跑并保存派生版本。
dsh-science-workbench 的功能「项目与产物浏览」：工作台展示分析步骤和产物详情，支持检索 cell 并预览生成的图表。
dsh-science-workbench 的功能「研究绘图规范」：附带 figure-style 与 figure-composer 技能，提供单图规范及多面板组合流程。
dsh-science-workbench 使用前须知：项目初始化会创建项目目录、manifest、环境快照和本地 Git 仓库；cell 产物与每次运行记录保存在配置的 projects root 中。

A **reproducible science workbench** plugin for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It blends the best of three worlds:

- **Jupyter** — cells and inline figures you can see and re-run;
- **Claude Science** — an agent as the execution engine;
- **Nextflow / nf-core** — every artifact carries full provenance.

dsh-science-workbench README · dsh-science-workbench：> **Core promise**: every figure and artifact is traceable and replayable. You can always answer *“it = which code + which inputs + which environment + which params/seed”*, and re-run it in one click.

---

dsh-science-workbench README · ✨ Features：- **Code → figure → feedback → redraw** — the agent runs a self-contained cell to produce figures shown inline; you attach structured feedback to a figure, and `bio_rerun_cell` regenerates a derived version (`v1 → v2 → v3`).
- **One ledger per project** — a plain-text `manifest.json` is the single source of truth: cells, artifacts, provenance and feedback history.
- **Reproducible by construction** — self-contained scripts, a fresh subprocess per cell, `environment.lock`, SHA-256 input/output hashes and a fixed seed.
- **Git-versioned automatically** — each project is `git init`-ed on creation and auto-committed at every step (never pushed).
- **Cross-platform** — the Host shell layer speaks bash on macOS/Linux and PowerShell on Windows; Python resolves to `python` on Windows and `python3` on POSIX.

dsh-science-workbench README · 🛠 Tools：| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bio_init_project` | Create/open a project: `code/ data/ figures/` + `manifest.json` + `environment.lock` + `git init`. |
| `bio_run_cell` | Run one self-contained cell, discover figures, register artifacts with hashes, commit. |
| `bio_rerun_cell` | Re-run a cell with edited code as a derived version (lineage recorded). |
| `bio_add_feedback` | Attach structured feedback to an artifact (this is how a “redraw it” note becomes history). |
| `bio_get_project` | Return a project summary: cells, artifacts, provenance and feedback. |
| `bio_list_projects` | List all projects under the projects root. |
| `bio_set_projects_dir` | Set the root directory where projects live (persisted across restarts). |
| `bio_delete_cell` | Delete a cell and its produced artifacts (script + figures). |
| `bio_mark_cell` | Mark a cell as a final (成品) artifact, or unmark it — flagged in the workbench and index. |

dsh-science-workbench README · 🛠 Tools：The **“Analysis workbench”** tab shows the notebook, artifacts, provenance and feedback in a three-panel UI with inline figure preview (PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF/TIFF/BMP), a **searchable project picker** (filter by name, sorted by most-recent activity), a **cell search box**, a **native directory picker** for the projects root, and a **mark-as-final** badge on completed cells. Very large figures (multi-MB) load on demand and display in full.

dsh-science-workbench README · 🛠 Tools：The plugin also bundles two **publication-grade figure skills** (adapted from Claude Science, Apache-2.0): `figure-style` (figure correctness & legibility rules + `apply_figure_style()`) and `figure-composer` (multi-panel figure composition with an adversarial self-review loop). See `skills/` and [ATTRIBUTIONS.md](./ATTRIBUTIONS.md).

dsh-science-workbench README · 📸 Feature showcase：The **feedback → redraw loop** — every figure keeps its structured feedback history, and a one-click “让 agent 重画” (let the agent redraw) produces a derived version.

The workbench tab — a three-panel layout: the **analysis steps** list (with status and lineage `cell_0001 → cell_0001_v2 → cell_0001_v3`) on the left, and the **artifact detail** (inline figure + provenance / code tabs + script / delete / Finder actions) on the right.

dsh-science-workbench README · 📸 Feature showcase：The **code** tab — every artifact’s generating script carries its declaration header (cell / title / language / seed / params / inputs), so it can be reviewed and reused at any time.

The **provenance** tab — full provenance: producing cell, output SHA-256 hash, params, seed, derived-from and created time.

dsh-science-workbench README · 📦 Install：`dsh-science-workbench` is a dual-face DSH plugin (Host + Client). Install it with the standard `dsh plugin` command — a thin pnpm forwarder that installs the package into a profile and **automatically adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles`** (because the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`).

```bash
dsh-science-workbench README · From npm (published):：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-science-workbench

dsh-science-workbench README · Local development (from a checkout):：dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-science-workbench
```

Then restart `dsh web`. The `bio_*` tools become globally available, the workbench tab appears, and the plugin shows up under **Settings → Plugins**.

dsh-science-workbench README · DSH desktop app：The desktop app owns its own `desktop` profile, which the `dsh` CLI refuses to write (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`). Install from inside the app instead:

dsh-science-workbench README · DSH desktop app：1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar.
2. **Add plugin** → paste the package name (`dsh-science-workbench`) or the absolute path of a checkout (`/path/to/dsh-science-workbench`) → **Install** → **Enable now**.
3. Restart the app so the Host half loads (module hot-reload deliberately ignores `node_modules`, so a linked checkout is not picked up while running).

dsh-science-workbench README · DSH desktop app：Projects may live outside the app's session workspace — point the plugin at your own root with `bio_set_projects_dir` (e.g. `~/bio-projects`); file writes are not fenced to the session workspace.

dsh-science-workbench README · 🚀 Quick start：After installing and restarting, just ask the agent in plain language:

> “帮我用 `demo_tss` 项目画一个 TSS 附近的信号热图。”

The agent will drive the tools for you. The equivalent manual flow is:

```text
1. bio_init_project { name: "demo_tss" }
2. bio_run_cell { title: "TSS profile", code: "..." }   # writes figures/*.png
3. look at the inline figure → bio_add_feedback { artifactPath, text: "把配色改成 Blues" }
4. bio_rerun_cell { cellId: "cell_0001", editedCode: "..." }  # → cell_0001_v2 + new figure

dsh-science-workbench README · 🚀 Quick start：Every step is committed to the project’s git history and recorded in `manifest.json`, so the whole lineage (`cell_0001 → cell_0001_v2 → …`) stays inspectable.

dsh-science-workbench README · 🧩 Architecture：- **Host** (`lib/index.js`) is the single source of truth. It registers the `bio_*` tools into the host `tools` registry, does all execution/provenance, and serves the `/biowb/*` data routes through the `webServer` service.
- **Client** (`lib/client.js`) is a pure projection — a hand-written browser bundle that reads/writes over same-origin `fetch('/biowb/<method>')`. No typert Remote bridge and no harness monorepo build are required.
- The **convention skill** (`skills/bio-workbench`) teaches the agent the project layout, the cell contract and the feedback loop.

|---|---|---|

| Hash | `shasum -a 256` | `Get-FileHash` |
| mkdir / move / delete | `mkdir -p` / `mv` / `rm -f` | `New-Item` / `Move-Item` / `Remove-Item` |
| Open in file manager | `open` / `open -R` | `explorer.exe` / `explorer.exe /select,` |
| Python | `python3` | `python` |

dsh-science-workbench README · 📦 Releasing：Publishing runs on **npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)** — `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
fires on a `v*` tag and exchanges the GitHub Actions OIDC token for publish
rights. **No npm token is stored in this repo or in CI secrets.**

dsh-science-workbench README · 📦 Releasing：One-time setup, on npmjs.org (not in the repo): *Package → Settings → Trusted
Publisher → GitHub Actions*, with `poplarity` / `dsh-science-workbench` /
`publish.yml` (the **basename**, not `.github/workflows/publish.yml`) and an empty
environment. npm matches those claims exactly; a mismatch comes back as a `404`
on `PUT`, which reads like a permissions error but is a config mismatch.

To cut a release:

```bash

dsh-science-workbench README · 2. bump version in package.json：git commit -am "v0.3.2: ..."
git tag -a v0.3.2 -m v0.3.2          # tag must equal v<package.json version>
git push origin main && git push origin v0.3.2
```

The workflow fails fast if the tag does not match `package.json`, checks the
runner's npm is ≥ 11.5.1, publishes with `--provenance`, then re-reads the
registry to confirm the version is live **and** carries a provenancebash
npm view dsh-science-workbench@<version> --json | jq .dist.attestations
```

dsh-science-workbench README · 2. bump version in package.json：> npm 10.x is not sufficient: the OIDC handshake still succeeds and a provenance
> attestation is produced, but the publish request goes out without OIDC auth
> headers and is rejected with `404`. Node 24 (npm 11.x) clears this.
